title: CPMigrate Output
description: The payload CPMigrate writes under --output Json. Consumers should key off outputSchemaVersion rather than the tool version: field additions bump the minor, and the only field whose meaning has ever changed is documented in the CHANGELOG. Four payload shapes exist: a single operation, the aggregate --batch writes, and the two --why package-origin reports — one package per document, or several under operation why-many. They are distinguished by `operation`, or by the presence of `solutions`.

outputSchemaVersion.description: Version of this contract, independent of the tool version. Additive changes bump the minor; a field changing meaning is called out in the CHANGELOG.

version.description: CPMigrate version that produced the payload

success.description: Whether the operation completed without a failure. Note that findings below the --fail-on threshold leave this true — check summary.issuesFound to see whether anything was reported at all.

exitCode.description: Process exit code. 0 clean, 5 findings at or above the gate, 8 an incomplete scan — see the exit-code table in the README.

fixes.description: Changes written by --fix, or proposed by --fix-dry-run

dryRun.description: Whether the run was a preview and wrote nothing

timestamp.description: When the operation completed, in ISO 8601

singleOperation.description: A single operation's result. Emitted by every command except --batch.

batchOperation.description: Emitted by --batch, which aggregates one result per solution rather than describing a single operation. A consumer distinguishes the two shapes by `operation`, or by the presence of `solutions`.

version.description: CPMigrate version that produced the payload

operation.description: Which batch command produced the payload

success.description: Whether every solution succeeded. A single failing solution makes this false, regardless of --batch-continue.

solutions.description: One entry per solution, in discovery order

baselineStaleEntries.description: Batch-wide count of baseline entries that matched no finding in any solution — accepted debt that has since been fixed. Fingerprints identify projects relative to their scan root, so this verdict assumes the baseline was recorded against the same solution roots the batch used; mixed-root workspaces should confirm per solution. Null when no baseline was used, it could not be read, or the batch stopped early: a partial run cannot tell live debt from fixed debt.

baselineUnknownRuleCodes.description: Rule IDs the baselines cite that no current rule publishes, across the whole batch. Absent under the same conditions as baselineStaleEntries.

summary.description: Counts for the operation. Fields not relevant to the command that ran are omitted rather than zeroed, so their absence is meaningful.

issuesFound.description: Every finding reported, including ones below the --fail-on threshold and ones a baseline accepted

failOnSeverity.description: The configured failure threshold, so a consumer can tell a clean run from one whose findings were below the gate

issuesAtOrAboveThreshold.description: The subset of findings the exit code reflects

issuesRemainingAfterFixes.description: Findings still present after --fix wrote its changes, from a fresh scan. Absent when no fixes were applied; issuesFound stays as the pre-fix count so it lines up with the fixes array.

issuesBaselined.description: Findings a baseline accepted, and therefore excluded from the gate. Absent when no baseline was used.

baselineStaleEntries.description: Baseline entries that matched no finding this run — accepted debt that has since been fixed. They suppress nothing, so a non-zero count means those entries can be removed from the baseline file by hand — do not use --write-baseline for this, as it also accepts every new finding the run reported. Absent when no baseline was used.

baselineUnknownRuleCodes.description: Rule IDs the baseline cites that no current rule publishes — usually renamed or deleted rules rather than fixed debt. Run 'cpmigrate --explain all' for the current rule IDs. Empty or absent when every entry names a live rule.

disabledRules.description: Rules switched off by the --rules policy or the config file's rules map. Their findings are absent from analysisIssues entirely, so this is what distinguishes a clean solution from one whose findings were configured away. Absent when no rule was disabled.

severityOverrides.description: Rules whose severity was re-graded before the gate was applied, keyed by rule ID. Without it, a severity in analysisIssues could not be reconciled with the one the rule documentation publishes. Absent when no rule was re-graded.

scanFailures.description: Projects that could not be scanned. Non-zero means the findings are incomplete, and exitCode is 8.

deepScanFailures.description: Opt-in package queries (--audit/--outdated/--deprecated/--licenses) that failed to return

packagesHeldBack.description: Accepted updates that did not survive verification and were left at their old version

verificationRuns.description: Restore+test cycles executed, which is what --bisect spends

bisectBudgetExhausted.description: Whether bisection stopped early on its run budget, leaving some updates unresolved

type.description: Display name of the analyzer that reported the finding

issueCode.description: Stable rule identifier, the same value SARIF uses as ruleId. Explain one with: cpmigrate --explain <issueCode>

affectedProjects.description: Projects the finding affects, each as a path relative to the scan root and forward-slashed, so the value is identical on every machine. Before schema 1.3.0 these were bare file names.

fixable.description: Whether a built-in fixer addresses this finding

suppressed.description: Whether a baseline accepted this finding. Suppressed findings are still reported but excluded from the gate.

metadata.description: Analyzer-specific detail; keys vary by rule

applied.description: False under --fix-dry-run, and for a fix that failed to write

heldBack.description: Excluded because it broke verification, and left at its old version

verification.description: The resolved-graph receipt a --verify migration produces. Absent when --verify was not passed, so a run that never verified stays distinguishable from one that verified and found nothing. Added in output schema 1.5.0.

verdict.description: 'failed' means no verdict could be reached — restore failed, or the two captures do not describe the same solution. Never read it as clean: not knowing is not the same as knowing nothing is wrong.

passed.description: Whether the run was allowed to stand, after --verify-strict is applied. This is what exit code 9 reflects.

strict.description: Whether --verify-strict was in force. Under it, drift the report can explain still fails.

rolledBack.description: Whether the migration was undone. False for a strict-only failure, where the tree is deliberately left in place to be read.

projectsRestored.description: Projects whose graph was read after the migration.

projectsExpected.description: Projects the baseline covered. A smaller projectsRestored is why a verdict can be 'failed' with no changes listed.

resolvedVersions.description: Total resolved package versions compared, across every project and target framework.

unexplained.description: Changes nothing the migration decided accounts for. Any non-zero value fails the run.

failureReason.description: Why no verdict could be reached. Absent unless verdict is 'failed'.

decisions.description: Which version won for each conflicted package, out of what, and at whose direction. summary.conflictsResolved is only a count and cannot answer any of those.

integrityFailures.description: Why the two graphs could not be compared. Absent when they could.

direction.description: 'downgrade' is the one to gate on hardest: it is how a migration silently reverts a fix only one project had picked up.

direct.description: Whether the project references this package itself, as opposed to receiving it through another.

causedBy.description: The package this change was reached from in the resolved graph. Absent unless explanation is 'transitiveFallout'.

source.description: 'interactive' only when a prompt was actually answered; a non-TTY falls back to the configured strategy and is recorded as that.

targetFramework.description: Absent when the whole project, rather than one framework, is the problem.

solutionResult.description: One solution's outcome within a batch. Carries its own exit code and summary, so a partially failing batch can be diagnosed per solution.

name.description: Solution file name without its extension

exitCode.description: This solution's exit code, using the same table as a single-solution run

error.description: Present when the solution threw rather than returning a result

propsFile.description: Path to the generated props file, for migrate mode

whyReport.description: The answer `--why <PACKAGE_ID> --output Json` prints instead of the console tree: where one package comes from across the workspace. Exit codes match the terminal mode exactly, and exitCode mirrors them so parsing stdout alone gives the same verdict as reading $?.

operation.description: Always 'why'; distinguishes this shape from singleOperation and batchOperation

packageId.description: The package asked about, as it was passed

status.description: 'found' when any project declares or sees the package

exitCode.description: Process exit code, mirrored from the run: 0 found with a complete scan, 1 not found with every project read, 8 part of the workspace could not be scanned

versionsInUse.description: Every distinct resolved version and its projects; more than one entry is version drift

suggestions.description: Near-miss package names present in the workspace, for a misspelled ID

whyManyReport.description: The answer `--why A,B,C --output Json` prints instead of the console banners: every package's answer over one shared workspace scan. exitCode mirrors the process exit code — the worst of the per-package answers (any incomplete scan → 8, else any not-found → 1, else 0); each result also carries its own code so a caller can tell which package drove it.

operation.description: Always 'why-many'; distinguishes this shape from singleOperation, batchOperation, and the single-package whyReport

packageIds.description: The packages asked about, as they were passed, in order

exitCode.description: Process exit code, mirrored from the run: 0 every package found over a fully-read workspace, 1 some package not found, 8 part of the workspace could not be scanned — see the exit-code table in the README

results.description: One answer per asked-about package, in the order the IDs were passed

whyAnswer.description: One package's answer inside a whyManyReport: the same per-package fields whyReport carries, minus the document-level ones

packageId.description: The package asked about, as it was passed

status.description: 'found' when any project declares or sees the package

exitCode.description: The code this package's answer settles on, mapped exactly as a single-package run would map it

versionsInUse.description: Every distinct resolved version and its projects; more than one entry is version drift

suggestions.description: Near-miss package names present in the workspace, for a misspelled ID

projectPath.description: Full path to the project file, as scanned

relativePath.description: Path relative to the scan root, forward-slashed; a bare file name when no scan root is known

kind.description: The project's strongest relationship to the package

inlineVersion.description: Present only when kind is inlineVersion

resolvedVersions.description: Distinct normalized versions NuGet resolved here; absent when the project could not be read

versionsByTargetFramework.description: One resolved version per target framework, from this run's readable resolved graph; absent when no graph was available or the project's scans did not succeed

transitiveIntroducers.description: Direct packages that pull the target in; present only when kind is transitiveOnly, empty when no graph could name one

targetFramework.description: Short framework name, as the assets file keys it

direct.description: Projects declaring the package directly (inline or central pin)

updateOnly.description: Projects amending an inherited reference via PackageReference Update

transitive.description: Projects seeing the package only through another package's closure

inherited.description: Projects resolving top-level while declaring the package outside the project file

notPresent.description: Projects that neither declare nor see the package

unreadable.description: Projects that could not be examined

failedScans.description: How many scans failed — the number behind exit code 8
